input_policy: Ring-only inputs: red/infrared ring PPG, ring accelerometer and ring-derived transforms. No smartwatch, chest ECG, oximeter waveform, respiration band, reference HR/SpO2/RR, or clinical labels are predictors.

targets.rr: Respiratory-rate reference from synchronized respiratory instrumentation (or chest ECG-derived RR in the separate treadmill cohort).
targets.spo2: Synchronized reference SpO2; this is measurement estimation, not a disease diagnosis.

split: Five-fold GroupKFold by participant; all windows from a participant remain in one held-out fold. Ring types are evaluated separately.

archive_extraction.source_integrity_note: The Zenodo file checksum matches its record, but the source archive is missing its ZIP directory. This evaluation uses only the per-person tables recoverable by local ZIP repair and is therefore partial.

ring1_spo2.low_oxygen_task_note: The <90% subset is controlled hypoxia in volunteers, not a pulmonary disease cohort.

ring2_spo2.low_oxygen_task_note: The <90% subset is controlled hypoxia in volunteers, not a pulmonary disease cohort.

ring1_rr.validation: nested five-fold GroupKFold by participant; 3-fold inner GroupKFold selects among ridge, Extra Trees, random forest, and histogram gradient boosting; the outer participant fold is untouched until scoring

ring2_rr.validation: nested five-fold GroupKFold by participant; 3-fold inner GroupKFold selects among ridge, Extra Trees, random forest, and histogram gradient boosting; the outer participant fold is untouched until scoring

clinical_limitations: HealthRing contains healthy volunteers, not participants with COPD, asthma, pneumonia, or other confirmed pulmonary diagnoses.
Controlled low oxygen in volunteers is not equivalent to a pulmonary disease or a spontaneous exacerbation.
The dataset validates ring signal-to-vital estimation only; it cannot train or validate disease detection.
Performance on this custom research ring does not establish performance on an Oura, Samsung, or future PlumoRing device.
Reference measurements and participant-level uncertainty must be reviewed before any physiological estimate is shown as more than a research demonstration.
